title: Image production: acquisition, quality, and radiation
summary: How the mammography beam is made and shaped, how FFDM and DBT differ, how technologists judge image quality, and how to talk about radiation risk without inventing numbers.

visuals.title: Find the beam-limiting device
visuals.prompt: Select the beam-limiting device on this schematic unit.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Component A, top block on the C-arm
Component B, small block just below A
Component C, thin plate above the breast
Component D, base under the breast

feedback.a: That is the tube housing, where x-rays are produced.
feedback.b: Correct. The beam-limiting device shapes the field between the tube and the patient.
feedback.d: That is the breast support with the image receptor.

visuals.explanation: Along the beam: tube housing → beam-limiting device → compression paddle → breast → breast support and receptor. MQSA's unit definition includes generator, control, tube housing, beam-limiting device, and supports.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Components are described by position only until after you answer.

visuals.title: What does DBT reconstruct?
visuals.prompt: Select the part of the schematic that represents the thin reconstructed slice planes through the breast.

hotspots.neutralLabel: Region A, the tube arc above the breast
Region B, stacked horizontal lines inside the breast
Region D, the support table only

feedback.a: The arc shows tube positions during acquisition, not the reconstructed slices.
feedback.b: Correct. DBT assembles multiple thin-slice images into a 3D dataset.
feedback.c: The paddle compresses the breast; it is not the reconstructed volume.
feedback.d: The support holds the breast; the slices are the reconstructed planes inside tissue.

visuals.explanation: NCI describes DBT as acquiring multiple thin-slice pictures that software assembles into a 3D picture, while also creating 2D images.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Regions are announced by location; names appear after answering.

visuals.title: Which panel is shielding?
visuals.prompt: Select the ALARA panel that shows placing a barrier between you and the source.

hotspots.revealLabel: Shielding: barrier between you and source

feedback.a: That panel is time: finish the necessary work and leave.
feedback.b: That panel is distance: farther away means lower dose.
feedback.c: Correct. Shielding puts material between you and the source.
feedback.d: The banner labels the figure; it is not one of the three measures.

visuals.explanation: CDC's ALARA measures are time, distance, and shielding. In a clinic, standing behind a barrier while exposing is the everyday shielding example.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Panels are selectable by left/center/right position.

visuals.title: Which setup is magnification geometry?
visuals.prompt: Select the schematic that shows the breast raised above the receptor with an air gap.

feedback.a: Contact geometry places the breast on the receptor; there is no air gap.
feedback.b: Correct. Magnification raises the breast, creating OID and an air gap; MQSA requires the system can operate with the grid removed.
feedback.c: That is only the caption for the contact diagram.
feedback.d: That is only the caption; select the diagram itself.

visuals.explanation: MQSA requires magnification systems to provide at least one factor between 1.4 and 2.0 and to operate with the grid removed. The air gap replaces grid cleanup in that geometry.
visuals.accessibilityNote: Left versus right schematic can be chosen from the keyboard.

glossary.definition: X-rays produced when electrons decelerate in the anode (braking radiation).
X-ray emitted when an electron fills an inner-shell vacancy in an anode atom; energies identify the element.
3D mammography that acquires multiple thin-slice projections and reconstructs a volumetric image set; also produces 2D images.
Full-field digital mammography: a digital 2D mammographic modality under MQSA's modality definition.
As low as reasonably achievable: avoid non-beneficial radiation exposure; use time, distance, and shielding.
Conservative model assuming any increase in dose incrementally increases cancer risk; accepted by the NRC for radiation protection estimates.
SI unit of absorbed dose: 1 Gy = 1 J/kg = 100 rad.
SI unit of equivalent dose: Sv = Gy × RBE; 1 Sv = 100 rem.
Component that shapes the x-ray field; required part of a mammography unit under MQSA.
Space between the magnified breast and the receptor that reduces scatter reaching the detector when the grid is removed.
